svg.text: Personal Library — Frontend Component Interaction
Hand-rolled runtime: Component views • observable Stores • typed event bus • swappable adapters — no framework
Component / Data Flow
VIEW LAYER — Component subclasses (core/component.ts)
STATE LAYER — Store<S> subclasses (core/store.ts)
MESSAGING LAYER — services/backend (core/eventBus.ts)
ADAPTER LAYER — exactly one active at a time
BACKEND TIER

g.text: SUBSCRIBE / NOTIFY — the only path back up
coalesced into one microtask; setState() short-circuits
the dashed path is the Mock adapter — same contract, no network
SessionService renews on the dashed path: POST /auth/refresh

svg.text: CROSS-CUTTING TOPICS
'backend:adapter:changed' → appStore.scheduleFetch()
'backend:health:changed' • ':request:started' / ':settled'
Swapping the adapter needs no listener rebuild.
WHY AN EVENT BUS AT ALL
A direct store → adapter call would work, but every request would
then be invisible. Routing through topics makes the whole
conversation observable, lets the gateway time and normalise
errors in one place, and lets the adapter be swapped at runtime
without rebuilding a single subscription.
BackendGateway.execute() • services/backend/BackendGateway.ts
PROMISES OVER AN EVENT BUS
requestBackend() generates a requestId, subscribes to the
matching :success and :failure topics, publishes the request,
then resolves or rejects and disposes both listeners. Callers
write plain await; the message still crosses the bus. Envelopes
whose requestId does not match are ignored.
requestBackend() • services/backend/BackendGateway.ts
LIFECYCLE AND LEAK SAFETY
Every subscription is registered through Component.track(),
so destroy() disposes store listeners, bus listeners and timers
together. render() replaces innerHTML wholesale, then restores
focus and scroll from a snapshot — which is what keeps typing
in a filter field from losing the caret on a background refresh.
core/component.ts • track() / render() / destroy()
